## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | The pages read describe editor-led development rather than a referee process. Articles are "primarily solicited by the editorial team"; the editors "look at all unsolicited material" (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23). After a proposal is agreed, the first draft gets detailed comments from the editors and a full set of suggested edits from the managing editor, and there may be more than one round of comment and revision (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions). Neither page mentions external referees or a blind-review model; that absence is recorded, not read as proof that no outside readers are used |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source. The AEA's transfer option is documented for the AER and AER: Insights only (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aej/faq-transfer-option) |

| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source |

## Format

> Sources: https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions and https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy, read 2026-11-23. The pages describe proposals, not a manuscript template.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Articles that give original, opinionated perspectives on economic topics grounded in frontier scholarship, arguing for the author's view, explaining how recent theoretical or empirical work has affected it, and laying out points of departure from other views. The journal does not publish book reviews or literature reviews, and says highly mathematical papers, research-intensive papers on narrowly focused topics and papers inaccessible to the general AEA membership are not appropriate (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions) |
| **Word limit** | Blank. No word or page limit for the finished article is stated on the pages read. For proposals the page says "2-5 page article proposal" in one paragraph and "two- or three-page proposal" in another (same page) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No source |
| **Abstract limit** | Blank. No abstract rule on the pages read |
| **Reference limit** | Blank. No source |
| **Supplementary material** | The page says the author may leave a derivation "to another publication or to an appendix" (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions); no appendix rules are given |
| **Figure/Table limits** | Blank. No source |
| **Style / submission format** | Proposals and papers are sent as Word or PDF email attachments to the journal's email address printed on the page; the process is the same for full papers. The aim is articles readable by 90 percent or more of the AEA membership, with mathematical notation kept light and complexity explained for a general economist (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 282 works dated 2021-2026 (OpenAlex; works with at least one author in the country): United States 235, United Kingdom 41, Germany 23, France 11, Canada 10, Switzerland 8, Italy 6, Spain 4, Netherlands 4, Belgium 3, Denmark 3, Chile 2 (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.id:S72880728,publication_year:2021-2026&group_by=authorships.countries, retrieved 2026-11-23). One of the most-cited recent items is an article titled "LGBTQ Economics" (230 Crossref citations, https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.35.2.141). No editorial statement on these topics was read |

Most-cited items dated 2021-2026 in Crossref (citation counts at retrieval): The Evolution of Work from Home (386; https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.37.4.23), An Introductory Guide to Event Study Models (379; https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.37.2.203), The Importance of Financial Literacy: Opening a New Field (316; https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.37.4.137), Effects of the COVID-19 Recession on the US Labor Market: Occupation, Family, and Gender (270; https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.35.3.3). Behavioral or bias wording appears in 13 of 248 abstracts (5.2%) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a stated one. Articles should argue the author's point of view, explain how recent theoretical or empirical work has affected it, and set out points of departure from other views; the focus is "the central economic ideas of a question" and why it matters (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Articles written so that 90 percent or more of AEA members can read them, with intellectual "arbitrage" across subfields; the journal falls "considerably closer" to refereed research journals than to the popular press (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy).
- **Article type and length**: proposal of 2-5 pages preferred to a completed manuscript; no length limit for finished articles on the pages read (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: symposia sit inside regular issues; the current issue lists two (Economics of Higher Education; Private Debt) (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep, retrieved 2026-11-23). No open call for papers appears on the pages read.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: proposals that do not meet the editorial criteria get only a brief reply because of submission volume (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy). The page also says that "given the low chances that an unsolicited manuscript will be published", no one should write an unsolicited manuscript for the journal (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions). The two pages differ in tone: the editorial policy says the editors look at all unsolicited material.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: Crossref records 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23, 248 with abstract of 296 (83.8%); each count is the number of records with an abstract whose title or abstract matches the regex; share = count / 248. Scores follow this pass's own convention (0 = none; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was read). Scores measure how often a method is mentioned, not how editors treat it. The journal publishes synthesis, not new empirical research, so a method count here mostly reflects what an article surveys. The schema's rows come from other fields and several do not fit economics. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Disclosure statements must say whether IRB approval was obtained for the project and, if not, why (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records: 112 of 272 Crossref records with author lists (41.2%), 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The guidelines say that, with few exceptions, authors of published articles are researchers with a PhD in economics or a closely related field (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23). No independent-scholar rule is stated |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Papers with empirical work, simulations or experimental work must provide data, code and computation details before acceptance; all data must be legally acquired, and the editor may decline to publish a paper if data were not legally obtained (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | The pages read describe identified, editor-led exchange and ask for names with each proposal sent by email; no anonymization instruction appears (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23). The AER's anonymized-review trial covers the AER, AER: Insights and the four American Economic Journals and does not name the JEP (https://www.aeaweb.org/news/rct-announcement) |
| **AI use** | Disclose at submission; AI cannot be an author (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Free to read; no submission or publication fee mentioned on the pages read (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Unsolicited submissions** | See Framing Requirements: about 10-15 percent of published articles historically began as unsolicited proposals; a 2-5 page proposal is preferred to a manuscript; the editors look at all unsolicited material and also say the chances for an unsolicited manuscript are low (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions) |

**Read in a real browser 2026-11-24:** the 2026 Report of the Editor, Journal of Economic Perspectives (https://pubs.aeaweb.org/doi/pdfplus/10.1257/pandp.116.777), 3 pages. It opened as a PDF in the tab but the viewer exposes no page text, so the text was read by decoding the PDF's own text streams in the page (no external script, no file saved). It reports: 2025 total of 1,026 pages with 41 full-length articles and 6 features; about two million JEP article downloads from the journal site in 2025 and about 600,000 a year from JSTOR; a 2025 team of Heidi Williams (editor), Jonathan Parker and Jeffrey Kling (coeditors) and Timothy Taylor (managing editor). It contains no acceptance rate, no submission count and no timing.

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- Acceptance rate, desk rejection rate, timing: no figure on the pages read; the 2026 Report of the Editor was read in a real browser and holds none either.
- Peer-review model, reviewer list, preprint policy, word and abstract limits: not stated on the pages read.
- Reviewer competence variance, quantitative bias: no first-hand source.
- Impact factor, quartile, CiteScore: paywalled or not read, not stated by policy.

**Cross-language and forum checks performed (all returned zero journal-specific first-hand reports):**
- SciRev (English): journal page exists, popularity score 72.9 and an economics rank of 307 (Q2) printed there; the reviews page says there are currently no reviews (https://scirev.org/reviews/journal-of-economic-perspectives/).
- LetPub: a general search returned no JEP page; not checked directly.
- 小木虫 (muchong), 知乎 (zhihu), fabiaoji: one search in Chinese for JEP submission experience returned the AEA's own pages and two Chinese journal-information sites (basic details and an email-submission note), but no first-hand submission report. Those two sites were not opened.
- Reddit: a web search for the journal with "reddit", "unsolicited proposal", "submit experience" returned no Reddit thread; results were AEA pages and consultancy guides.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal does not publish book reviews or literature reviews, and says highly mathematical papers, research-intensive papers on narrowly focused topics and papers inaccessible to the general AEA membership are not appropriate (Format; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/editorial-policy).
- **Routing**: the guidelines say no one should write an unsolicited manuscript for the journal, and prefer a 2-5 page proposal (Framing Requirements; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions). Sending a manuscript is allowed by the same page but goes against its stated preference.
- **AI authorship**: AI software may not be listed as an author, and AI use must be described at submission (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker follows from a fact read: no word limit, fee or anonymization rule appears on the pages read.

### Soft Tax

- **Odds**: about 10-15 percent of published articles historically began as unsolicited proposals, and the guidelines call the chances for an unsolicited manuscript low (Framing Requirements). This is a share of published articles, so no acceptance rate can be derived.
- **Revision effort**: agreement on the article's shape may take one or more iterations; the author then gets several months for a draft, followed by detailed editor comments, a full set of managing-editor edits and possibly more rounds (Peer Review; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions).
- **Audience**: articles must be readable by 90 percent or more of AEA members, which means translating technical material (Framing Requirements).
- **Time**: no timing figure exists on the pages read or in the 2026 Report of the Editor (Review Cycle Time).

### Best Suited For

- Established researchers (a PhD in economics or a closely related field is the stated norm) who can write a synthesis with a point of view: "with few exceptions" (Practical Concerns; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/jep/submissions).
- Topics broad enough for a general economist, for instance the themes seen in the most-cited recent articles (work from home, event-study methods, financial literacy, the COVID-19 labour market) (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Sole authors: 112 of 272 Crossref records with author lists (41.2%) (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Original empirical or formal research papers: the journal says research-intensive and highly mathematical papers do not fit (Format), and field-experiment and structural-model wording is rare or absent in abstracts (5 and 0 of 248) (Methodological Preferences).
- Book or literature reviews: stated exclusion (Format).
- Qualitative or philosophical methodology work: interview or qualitative wording in 2 of 248 abstracts and philosophy wording in 0 (Methodological Preferences, Orientation). The counts show these are rare, not that they are rejected.
- Authors who need an acceptance rate or turnaround before choosing: none is printed on the pages read, nor in the 2026 Report of the Editor read in a real browser (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where declined proposals usually go. The rows below are topical or publisher neighbours listed only because they share a subject area or publisher; they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [American Economic Review](american-economic-review.md) | Same publisher; a refereed general-interest research journal with its own entry in this corpus. Suits an original research paper rather than a synthesis (see that entry's Format and Peer Review) |
| 2 | [Journal of Economic Methodology](journal-of-economic-methodology.md) | Entry exists in this corpus; shares the economics subject area. No fit evidence collected here |
